title: CS50 Pset5 trouble freeing memory leak caused by malloc
body_html:
i am new to stack-overflow so bare with me

I am taking CS50 and im on Pset5(speller) My code works as intended, however when I run the check50 function my program fails Valgrind, Valgrind doesn't find the leak without adding -s. I am sure it has something to do with freeing malloc on line 94 but still uncertain as to where i have gone wrong.

if you can assist me in resolving this issue i would much appreciate it.

link to CS50 Pset5: https://cs50.harvard.edu/x/2023/psets/5/speller/

See below to see code:

{

    const int p = 29;
    const int m = 1e6 + 9;

        //modulo keeps integer overflow to a minimum
        p_pow = (p_pow * p) % m;

}

        if (n == NULL)

         //
         table[hash_value] = n;
        }

    }
    //free up system resources that are using the file once finished
    fclose(file);
    return true;

}

// Returns number of words in dictionary if loaded, else 0 if not yet loaded
unsigned int size(void)
{
    // return the size of dictionary

    }

// Unloads dictionary from memory, returning true if successful, else false

{
    // to free memory used by malloc

events.body_html: Please edit your question to show us a proper minimal reproducible example. How are you using the functions you currently show? Where's your simple testing main function?

The loop in unload returns after freeing the first chain of nodes. You should remove that code. It also doesn't make much sense to return true or false there. There's no success or failure case in that function.

The implementation of unload() should be

void unload(void) {
    for(int i = 0; i < N; i++) {
        node *cursor = table[i];
        while (cursor != NULL) {
            node *tmp = cursor;
            cursor = cursor->next;
            free(tmp);
        }
    }
 }
  1. The function should return nothing instead of bool according to your logic.
  2. The return inside of while loop terminate the for loop in its first iteration. Then the elements[1...n - 1] of table aren't freed, causing the memory leak.

OT Hint: When adding words (from a dictionary presumed to be sorted), the first word in any chain at a given hash value will be the "largest value" word in the list... When searching along that linked list for, for example, "dogg", you can stop the search (not found) when you encounter "cat" (or whatever word would preceed the absent "dogg". No need to keep comparing against "bat" and "aardvark"...

thank you for replying comprehensively, this was my initial thought but due to the distribution code given by CS50 unload must remain a bool function, however you did help me find the solution by informing me of the shortfall of my for loop :)
